public_rationale: Anthropic's filing reports Q2 revenue that rounds to $11.6 billion. The number is corroborated, but its unspecified accounting basis prevents a decisive monetary score under the required rules. The broader assertion that AI companies never disclose actual revenue or economics is not established. The October filing cannot retroactively contradict the September statement about disclosure practices.
limitations: The quarterly filing data are unaudited.
The claim combines a specific financial amount with an unbounded disclosure generalization.
Investor communications and press reporting are not automatically direct public disclosures.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Anthropic's actual revenue in Q2 2026 was $11.6 billion, and AI companies do not disclose actual revenues or underlying economics.

statement.excerpt: AI companies never share their actual revenues — $11.6 billion in Q2 2026 — or their underlying economics, and reporters have been so systemically-sedated that they believe that using a marketing number is reporting.

from_speaker: AI companies never share their actual revenues
our_interpretation: The nearby Anthropic discussion identifies Anthropic as the company associated with the quarterly figure.
Q2 2026 means realized revenue for April through June 2026, rounded to one decimal billion dollars.
In context, AI companies primarily means standalone frontier AI developers. Expanding it to every public company selling AI would stretch the claim.
The disclosure assertion concerns public company disclosures available when the post appeared. Investor-only sharing and press leaks are distinct from direct public disclosure.

The numerical target period is Q2 2026. A later statement may verify that quarter's revenue, but a later disclosure event cannot retroactively contradict the September description of disclosure practices.
The passage gives no accounting basis or attribution for the $11.6 billion figure. Its basis is recorded as unknown rather than assumed to be GAAP.
criteria.support_condition: A matching quarterly revenue measure rounds to $11.6 billion, and a sufficiently complete review establishes the claimed absence of public realized-revenue and underlying-economics disclosures among the relevant companies before the post.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A matching quarterly revenue measure does not round to $11.6 billion, or a relevant company had publicly disclosed actual revenue or underlying economics before the post. Each component must retain its own period and accounting scope.
